correctness.rationale: Starting from Horváth's exact two-facet prism expression and visibility interval, convexity in the second coordinate reduces the maximum to the two endpoints. The upper endpoint is at most \(1-1/n^2\). The lower endpoint becomes the Rayleigh quotient of the displayed \(2\times2\) symmetric matrix, whose largest eigenvalue is exactly the stated radical after direct characteristic-polynomial calculation. The positive eigenvector satisfies the strict second-facet visibility inequality, and the explicit normal construction makes all other facets non-upper, so the relaxation is realizable. Independent eigenvalue calculations for \(3\le n<30\) reproduce the closed expression, while the bundled checker verifies the same geometry through \(n=400\). The finite checks corroborate rather than replace the analytic proof.
